issues.legal_issue: A general-area designation that activates an existing statutory scheme does not, without an express requirement or other indication, imply a duty to give affected persons a prior hearing.
material_facts: The designation brought an area containing a factory within the territorial reach of an existing statutory scheme.
The governing enactment did not require prior publication of the proposal or consideration of public representations before the designation.
No prior opportunity to make representations was given.
issues.conclusion: The designation was not invalid for failure to provide a prior hearing; the audi alteram partem rule did not apply by necessary implication.
issues.legal_principle: Natural justice ordinarily requires notice and a fair opportunity to make representations when an administrative decision affects individual rights. But the court classified this power as legislative in character: the designation made an existing statutory scheme applicable to a geographical area and was conditional legislation. In the absence of an express hearing requirement, audi alteram partem does not apply by necessary implication to that legislative function. The court distinguished A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India, Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner, Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, and Schmidt v. Secretary of State for Home Affairs as involving administrative action directed against persons; it also relied on Bates v. Lord Hailsham for the distinction between legislative and administrative functions.

predicates.challenge_to_area_designation: A proceeding challenges a decision that brings a geographical area within an existing statutory scheme.
predicates.designation_activates_existing_general_s: The decision makes an existing body of law applicable to the area rather than adjudicating an individual's rights in a dispute.
predicates.no_express_prior_hearing_requirement: The governing law does not expressly require advance notice or a hearing before the area is designated.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges an area designation that activates an existing general scheme and the governing law does not expressly require a prior hearing, the designation may stand without an implied prior hearing.

issues.legal_issue: A designation that determines where an existing statutory scheme will apply is conditional legislation rather than subordinate legislation.
material_facts: The enactment established the statutory scheme, while the designation determined the geographical area to which that scheme would apply.
The designation did not make rules under the separate rule-making power.
The challenger argued that the designation had to follow the procedure prescribed for making rules.
issues.conclusion: The designation was conditional legislation, not subordinate legislation, and the procedure for making rules did not apply to it.
issues.legal_principle: Conditional legislation occurs where the legislature has prescribed the law and an authority determines whether or where it will operate; it is distinct from delegated or subordinate legislation that makes rules under delegated authority. The court relied on The Queen v. Burah, King v. Benoari Lal Sharma, In re The Delhi Laws Act, Baxter v. Ah Way, Basant Kumar Sarkar v. Eagle Rolling Mills, and Bangalore Woollen, Cotton and Silk Mills Co. Ltd. v. Corporation of the City of Bangalore. It also held that the rule-making procedure in section 39(3) of the U.P. Town Area Act, 1914 did not apply to a designation under section 3.

predicates.challenge_to_area_designation: A proceeding challenges a decision applying a statutory scheme to a geographical area.
predicates.legislature_prescribes_existing_scheme: The legislature itself has established the legal scheme that will operate once the relevant condition is met.
predicates.authority_only_determines_area_of_operat: The authority's decision determines where the existing scheme applies rather than creating rules under delegated law-making authority.

issues.definition: Where a proceeding challenges an area designation, the legislature has prescribed the scheme, and the authority only determines its territorial operation, the designation is conditional rather than subordinate legislation.

issues.legal_issue: Official publication of an area's designation is conclusive proof of the determination that the area is not an agricultural village when the governing enactment makes that publication conclusive.
material_facts: The designation was published in the official gazette.
The challenger asserted that the area was part of an agricultural village and therefore could not be included.
The governing enactment made the government's determination on that status, evidenced by the gazette publication, final and conclusive.
issues.conclusion: The agricultural-village challenge failed because the official publication was conclusive proof of the government's determination.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(2) of the U.P. Town Area Act, 1914 made the government's decision that an inhabited area was not an agricultural village final and conclusive, and made publication of a designation in the Official Gazette conclusive proof of that decision.

predicates.challenge_to_area_designation: A proceeding challenges the inclusion of an area in a designated town area.
predicates.official_publication_of_area_designation: The decision including the area was published in the official gazette.
predicates.law_makes_publication_conclusive_on_vill: The governing law makes that publication conclusive proof that the area does not have the excluded agricultural-village status.

issues.definition: If an area designation is challenged, it was officially published, and the governing law makes publication conclusive on the area's village status, that status cannot defeat the designation.

issues.legal_issue: An omission of territorial boundaries from a tax notification does not invalidate the levy when the intended local area is clear from the notification and existing designation, the proposed levy was published for objections, and the boundaries are later supplied consistently with that designation.
material_facts: A draft of the tax rules was published and invited objections and representations to the proposed levy.
The final notification identified the local area in which the tax was to operate and included a schedule of tax rates, but omitted a second schedule referring to the area's boundaries.
The boundaries had already been set out in a valid area designation, so there was no real doubt about the local area covered by the levy.
A later notification inserted the same boundaries into the tax notification.
The governing enactment made the published final notification conclusive proof that the tax had been imposed in accordance with the Act.
issues.conclusion: The omission of the second schedule was an inconsequential mistake; the tax notification was valid and effective, and the later notification could supply the boundaries.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 39(2) and 39(3) of the U.P. Town Area Act, 1914 governed the making and prior publication of tax rules; section 15B(4) made the published notification conclusive proof that the tax was imposed in accordance with the Act. The court held that the omission did not defeat the levy because the notification identified the local area, the boundaries were established by the existing area designation, the public had been invited to object to the proposed levy, and the later insertion matched those boundaries.

rule.if: challenge_to_local_tax_levy and draft_levy_published_for_objections and final_levy_notification_published and local_area_unambiguously_identifiable and omitted_boundaries_later_supplied_consistently

predicates.challenge_to_local_tax_levy: A proceeding challenges a local tax imposed by a published notification.
predicates.draft_levy_published_for_objections: A draft setting out the proposed tax rules was published and the public was invited to object or make representations.
predicates.final_levy_notification_published: The final tax notification was officially published.
predicates.local_area_unambiguously_identifiable: The notification and an existing valid area designation leave no real doubt about the local area in which the tax applies.
predicates.omitted_boundaries_later_supplied_consis: A boundary schedule omitted from the final notification was later added with boundaries matching the existing valid area designation.

issues.definition: When a published local tax levy followed publication of a draft for objections, the covered area is clear, and omitted boundaries are later supplied consistently with an existing designation, the omission does not invalidate the levy.
